purpose: Record the research and staged support experiment after the initial density screen.

sources.supports: Top interface spacing controls the space between interface lines; zero requests solid. Interface layer count, pattern and support ironing are separate controls.
Dense interface layers provide a more uniform landing surface and reduce sagging. Z contact distance controls separation. Generic recommendations do not select a PET-GF/Bambu setting.

sources.scope: General material guidance; the current profile's first-layer and local bridge cooling are established local treatments, held common in this screen.

initial_screen.reason: Isolate interface density with a current-spacing control while retaining the existing tree-support release gap.
initial_screen.inference: The denser mat may support the first roof course better; successful peel and retained surface quality remain unmeasured.
initial_screen.physical_result: All coupons self-release from supports during cooling; retained roof strands remain separate and locally projecting. No acceptable candidate.

next_comparison.priority: D transfer to reduced anchoring and representative pad contact
next_comparison.selection_basis: D and E retain the first roof layer during removal in the enclosed fixture; Derek explicitly selects D alone for the next plate.
scenarios: Larger cantilever with a model wall on one edge
Production holed-pad underside and wall root
next_comparison.intended_printer: Mark1 left fixed hardened Standard 0.4 mm, PET-GF

later_factors.trigger: The support mat itself remains uneven or fragile.
later_factors.reason: A thicker mat may distribute support and peel as a sheet; it also costs time and material and does not directly change contact gap.
Assess direction sensitivity, sag, wall-edge adhesion and practical removal access before transferring a flat short coupon result.

later_factors.trigger: An intact support mat releases, but the retained first model course remains loose.
later_factors.reason: Existing PET-GF bridge experiments support these candidates; they do not establish a universal winner for supported ceilings. Hold cooling and contact geometry common.

deferred_variables: Interface pattern, tree style, edge setback and ironing remain common during the first density/gap comparisons.
Nozzle temperature and general cooling remain common; screenshot suggestions for cooler printing do not establish a PET-GF process.
A different support filament needs its own material compatibility and nozzle arrangement experiment.
